subject: Knowledge-grounding eval follow-up + retrieval & reranker recommendations
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Ng <claire@hydratx.com>, Ben Walsh <ben.walsh@ben.walsh@hydratx.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-03T16:12:00Z
Subject: Knowledge-grounding eval follow-up + retrieval & reranker recommendations

Hi Claire / Ben — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a proposed short eval plan so we can validate model fit for your knowledge-grounding use case. I tried to keep this action-oriented.

What we heard (confirm if anything missing):
- Primary UX: agent-like answers surfaced on product pages + citations and document-level anchors.
- Quality bar: >92% grounding (source_in_span / grounded_answer) on your regulatory QA set; human-preference for factualness > baseline by +15% where policies matter.
- Latency target for prod reads: p95 under 600ms for single-turn queries.
- Data: ~120k docs (mixed PDFs + HTML), typical doc length 1–5 pages, 98% English.
- Constraint: procurement prefers a 1-week PoC before committing to reserved capacity.

Immediate recommendations (what we suggest to evaluate first):
1) Retriever: hybrid approach — dense vector retriever (Faiss HNSW, 1536-d) over chunked embeddings + BM25 lexical filter for precise recall. Start with chunk size 250 tokens, sliding window 50.
2) Reranker: light cross-encoder reranker (we recommend "rwx-crossenc-3m" for initial PoC) to improve grounding precision; for very tight latency budgets we can fallback to a fast bi-encoder score with a small accuracy loss.
3) Generation model: for the PoC we suggest the quantized 13B family (recommended profile: "rwk-13b-q4f") — good tradeoff of cost and instruction-following. If you need higher factual consistency, test the 33B profile next.
4) Grounding metrics: track two main signals — source_in_span (percentage of answers citing a source where the citation text contains the direct answer) and grounding_precision (precision@k of sentences selected by retriever+reranker). We'll provide a small eval harness to compute both.

Attached: hydra_prompt_set_v1.txt (sample prompts & negative prompts), hydra_retrieval_configs.json (starter retrieval + chunking settings), hydra_benchmarks_20260803.csv (seed benchmark rows). Also shared an internal drive eval plan (link below).

Proposed short PoC plan (1 week):
- Day 0: kickoff + data ingest checklist (we'll need a sample of 1k representative docs).
- Day 1–2: index with hybrid retriever, run baseline recall/precision.
- Day 3: run reranker experiments (rwX-crossenc-3m vs bi-encoder).
- Day 4: run generation with rwk-13b-q4f and compute grounding metrics + human spot-check.
- Day 5: deliver dashboard + recommendation and next-step pricing.

Next steps for you: confirm kickoff slot (we suggested Tue 8/11 10am PT) and share sample document bundle (S3 or Dropbox link). Once you confirm, we'll provision evaluation capacity and upload the starter configs.

Notes / known tradeoffs:
- RWK-13B quantized will be significantly cheaper but may show small drops on nuanced regulatory phrasing vs larger variants. We'll include prompt-tuning recommendations in the deliverable.
- Reranker adds ~40–70ms to p95; we can explore distillation for production to shrink that.

Let me know if you'd like me to prioritize lower latency (we'll push to a 7B family + heavier lexical filtering) or stricter grounding (move to 33B and stronger reranker).

Thanks — will follow-up with an updated plan after Claire/Ben questions.

—

Thanks Jonas — really helpful summary. A couple of clarifying questions before we lock the kickoff: 

1) Can you briefly explain how you compute "source_in_span"? We need to ensure it matches how our compliance team defines a cited source.
2) For the reranker you suggested, what is the typical p95 latency impact when used in the PoC? Our goal is to keep the demo responsive for reviewers.
3) Procurement asked if the PoC will require any data residency changes (we need to keep the sample data in US-only buckets).

Also, happy with the 1-week cadence — Tue 8/11 10am PT works for our team. We'll upload a 1k-doc sample to an S3 path and share credentials via Okta.

Finally: for the benchmarks you attached — is there a quick viewable dashboard we can glance at (rather than a CSV)? If not, the CSV is fine for now.

Cheers,
Claire
Head of Knowledge & Compliance | Hydra Therapeutics
claire@hydratx.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-05T13:02:00Z
Subject: FW: Knowledge-grounding eval follow-up + retrieval & reranker recommendations

Jonas / Sergio — forwarding Claire's clarifying questions with my proposed short answers so we can align before I respond: 

Q1: How do we compute source_in_span?
A1 (proposed): define source_in_span as: a returned citation is counted as positive if at least one contiguous sentence in the cited doc chunk has >=80% token overlap (after normalization) with the annotated ground-truth answer span. This matches how most regulatory QA sets are measured. We'll include code in the eval harness so Hydra can reproduce locally.

Q2: Reranker latency impact?
A2 (proposed): the cross-encoder RWX-crossenc-3M typically adds ~50–90ms p95 on our test infra at 16-token max scoring batches. For the PoC we can run it in a separate evaluation route so the interactive demo uses the fast bi-encoder path (small accuracy drop) and the evaluation route uses the cross-encoder to compute final grounding metrics.

Q3: Data residency?
A3 (proposed): PoC can run entirely in US-only regions; we'll confirm the infra team (ops) to ensure the evaluation hosts are pinned. No changes to the control plane necessary for one-week PoC.

Other internal notes:
- Pricing sensitivity: procurement will likely push back on anything that requires multi-region reserved capacity. Keep PoC as hosted eval capacity.
- We should propose an optional follow-up: a 2-week rig with 33B for legal review tasks, priced separately.

I'll draft a short reply to Claire consolidating these points. Sergio — please confirm the latency numbers on your end and if we should recommend a pre-filter threshold (I was thinking recall threshold 0.85 / top_k 30).

-Neha
Product Manager, Inference Evals | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Knowledge-grounding eval follow-up + retrieval & reranker recommendations

Claire / Ben — thanks for the quick reply and for confirming 8/11 10am PT. Below is a concise response to your questions and the finalized short PoC checklist.

Source_in_span (short): we'll provide an eval harness that marks a citation positive if at least one contiguous sentence in the cited chunk overlaps the annotated answer span by >=80% token overlap after normalization (lowercased, punctuation stripped). We'll include a README so your compliance team can validate the metric computation.

Reranker latency (short): expected p95 add of ~60ms for the recommended cross-encoder in our PoC infra. For the interactive demo we will route to a fast bi-encoder path and run the cross-encoder in the evaluation lane to compute final metrics; if Hydra prefers the cross-encoder live, we can estimate the cost/latency tradeoff and provide a tuned plan.

Data residency: confirmed — PoC evaluation hosts will be pinned to US regions only. We'll need your S3 path + Okta-approved credential exchange.

Finalized PoC checklist (we'll act on receipt of S3 sample + credential):
- Hydra: upload 1k sample docs to S3 + share path via Okta.
- Redwood: provision PoC index, apply hydra_retrieval_configs.json, run baseline retrieval and reranker experiments.
- Redwood: run generation with rwk-13b-q4f against hydra_prompt_set_v1.txt and compute grounding metrics.
- Redwood: share a small interactive demo link + dashboard (we'll include a short dashboard view and CSV export).

Attachments included in the PoC bundle: hydra_prompt_set_v1.txt, hydra_retrieval_configs.json, hydra_benchmarks_20260803.csv. Internal eval plan link: https://drive.redwood.internal/drive/1A2bHydraEvalPlan. Public benchmark preview: https://benchmarks.redwood.ai/hydra-DEAL-98721 (view-only).

Can you confirm when you'll share the S3 path? If everything looks good I'll send a calendar invite for 8/11 10am PT and loop in the ops contact for region pinning.

Appreciate it — looking forward to running this PoC.
